standard_prerequisites.name: Constructible sheaves are closed under finite limits and colimits
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the sheaves appearing in the constructions are constructible and that constructible sheaves of modules form an abelian category.

standard_prerequisites.name: Constructibility of the support of a map of constructible sheaves
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the loci where the maps on stalks fail to be isomorphisms constructible.

standard_prerequisites.name: The constructible topology on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is quasi-compact
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts pointwise eventual emptiness of a constructible subset into emptiness.

core_obligations: Case of sheaves of sets (proof lines 11922-11953): the locus where the map on stalks fails to be surjective is constructible and, the stalks being finite, is pointwise eventually empty, hence empty for large index by quasi-compactness of the constructible topology; the same argument applied to the sets measuring the failure of injectivity on the images gives the essential constancy.
Case of abelian sheaves (proof lines 11956-11957): a constructible abelian sheaf is in particular a constructible sheaf of sets, so this case follows from the first.

Case of modules (proof lines 11960-11987): using that constructible sheaves of modules form an abelian category, the supports of the cokernels are constructible and pointwise eventually empty, hence eventually empty, which gives surjectivity for large index; assuming surjectivity throughout, the same argument with the images of the kernels gives the factorization.
proof_roadmap: Prove the result for sheaves of sets by measuring the failure of surjectivity and of injectivity on constructible loci.
Deduce the abelian case from the case of sets.
Repeat the argument with cokernels and kernels in the abelian category of constructible modules.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves whose colimit is constructible is essentially constant, in the three settings of sheaves of sets, abelian sheaves and modules over a Noetherian ring (statement lines 11902-11919). The proof is a complete argument repeated in the three settings: the loci where the maps on stalks fail to be surjective, respectively fail to induce the same images, are constructible by the support result and are pointwise eventually empty because the stalks of a constructible sheaf are finite, so quasi-compactness of the constructible topology makes them empty for large index (proof lines 11922-11953); the abelian case reduces to the case of sets (proof lines 11956-11957); and the module case runs the same argument with cokernels and kernels inside the abelian category of constructible modules (proof lines 11960-11987). The non-formal content is the measurement of the failure of surjectivity and injectivity by constructible loci. The claim is H2: a written argument carried through three settings.
